body: ABDUL FAYAZ, J.- Through the instant criminal appeal, appellants Shah Bilal and Shah Sohail, both _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz sons of Muhammad Shah Faridoon, have called in question the judgment dated 25.09.2026 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-IV/Model Criminal Trial Court, Mansehra, whereby they were convicted and sentenced in case FIR No.430 dated 15.08.2021, registered under Sections 324/337-F(iii)/34 PPC at Police Station Saddar, Mansehra, as follows; (i) Appellant Shah Bilal was convicted under Section 324 PPC and sentenced to undergo seven years' rigorous imprisonment with a fine of Rs.50,000/-, and under Section 337-F(iii) PPC to undergo three years' rigorous imprisonment as Ta'zir, besides payment of Rs.100,000/- as Daman to injured Tasawar Nisar under Section 337-Y PPC.

(ii) Appellant Shah Sohail was likewise convicted under Section 324 PPC and sentenced to undergo seven years' rigorous imprisonment with a fine of Rs.50,000/-, and under Section 337-F(iii) PPC to undergo three years' rigorous imprisonment as Ta'zir, besides payment of Rs.100,000/- as Daman to injured Zohaib Nisar under Section 337-Y PPC.

The sentences of imprisonment were ordered to run concurrently, while both appellants were extended the benefit of Section 382-B Cr.P.C. The same occurrence also gave rise to cross-version Mad No.24 dated 15.08.2021, wherein accused Tasawar Nisar and Zohaib Nisar were acquitted through judgment of even date, against which Shah Bilal has filed connected Criminal Appeal No.196- A/2026, whereas complainant Tasawar Nisar has filed _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz the connected criminal revision seeking enhancement of the sentences awarded to the appellants. Since all three matters arise out of the same occurrence and involve common questions of fact and law, they are being decided together through this judgment.

2. Brief facts giving rise to the present proceedings are that on 15.08.2021, an occurrence took place between the parties at Khaitan-da-Galla, District Mansehra, against the background of a dispute concerning landed property. According to the prosecution, complainant Tasawar Nisar, along with his brother Zohaib Nisar, was present at his house when appellants Shah Bilal and Shah Sohail, allegedly armed with knives, arrived there. Shah Sohail is alleged to have inflicted knife blows upon Tasawar Nisar, causing injuries to his back and arm, whereas Shah Bilal allegedly inflicted knife blows upon Zohaib Nisar. The injured were shifted to the hospital, where their injuries were medically examined, and the matter was reported to the police, resulting in registration of FIR No.430 dated 15.08.2021 under Sections 324/337-F(iii)/34 PPC at Police Station Saddar, Mansehra.

Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz 3. The occurrence, however, was not confined to the version advanced by the complainant in the aforesaid FIR. On the same date, appellant Shah Bilal also reported the matter to the police through cross-version Mad No.24, alleging that Tasawar Nisar and Zohaib Nisar had attacked him and his brother with knives and caused bodily injuries. The said cross-version was registered under Sections 337-F(v)/337-F(ii)/337-A(i)/34 PPC. Thus, two rival versions of the same occurrence came before the investigating agency, each party attributing responsibility for the occurrence to the other. The existence of the cross-version, together with the injuries allegedly sustained by persons belonging to both sides, constituted an important circumstance requiring proper judicial consideration.

4. After completion of investigation, separate challans were submitted in the two cases. The proceedings arising out of Mad No.24 were initially instituted before the learned Judicial Magistrate and were subsequently transmitted to the Court of Sessions, whereas FIR No.430 was tried by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-IV/Model Criminal Trial Court, Mansehra. Although both cases originated from _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz the same transaction and involved the same contesting parties, their evidence was recorded separately. Upon conclusion of the proceedings, the learned trial Court convicted Shah Bilal and Shah Sohail in FIR No.430, while Tasawar Nisar and Zohaib Nisar, who faced trial in the cross-version, were acquitted through a separate judgment of the same date. The grievance of the appellants is that the learned trial Court failed to examine the two versions in their proper perspective and proceeded to determine criminal liability without bringing the material evidence of the connected proceedings onto the record of the main case.
5. Arguments of learned counsel for the parties as well as learned Astt: A.G. appearing on behalf of the State were heard in considerable detail and the record perused with their able assistance.

6. The pivotal question arising for determination is whether the conviction of the appellants can safely be sustained when two rival criminal cases emerged from the same occurrence, but the material evidence relating to cross-version Mad No.24 was not brought on record during the trial of FIR No.430. Since both parties attributed responsibility for the occurrence to each other and claimed to have sustained injuries, the determination _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz of criminal liability required careful examination of the genesis of the occurrence, the identity of the aggressor and the respective roles of the parties.

7. The record reveals that FIR No.430/2021 and cross-version Mad No.24, both dated 15.08.2021, arose from the same incident. The former was tried by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-IV/Model Criminal Trial Court, Mansehra, whereas proceedings in Mad No.24 were initially conducted before the learned Judicial Magistrate and subsequently transferred to the Court of Sessions. Although the investigation and trials in both cases have concluded, the evidence relating to Mad No.24 was not brought on record in the trial of FIR No.430/2021 in its complete form. Some documents concerning the cross-version were exhibited, but the relevant site plan, recovery memos, medical reports and other connected documents were not properly proved through their respective witnesses. Nor were the witnesses necessary to explain those documents examined. The learned trial Court, therefore, recorded the conviction without having before it the complete evidence relating to the rival version of the occurrence.

8. It is a settled principle of criminal law that an accused can be convicted only when the _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz prosecution establishes the charge through reliable and legally admissible evidence beyond reasonable doubt. The mere registration of a cross-case does not make the prosecution version doubtful, nor does the acquittal of the accused in one case necessarily justify the acquittal of the accused in the other. However, when both cases arise from the same occurrence and each party accuses the other of initiating the incident, the Court must examine the evidence relating to both versions to determine the true circumstances of the occurrence. This becomes particularly important where injuries have been sustained by persons on both sides. Unless the relevant evidence is properly examined, it may not be possible to determine with the required degree of certainty which party initiated the occurrence and whether the prosecution has established the role attributed to the accused.

9. The question of trying offences arising from the same transaction is governed by Sections 233 to 239 Cr.P.C. Section 235 Cr.P.C., in its relevant part, provides as follows:- “235. Offences committed in the course of the same transaction.—(1) If, in one series of acts so connected together as to form the same transaction, more offences than one are committed by the same person, he may be _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz charged with, and tried at one trial for, every such offence.

The above provision permits offences committed by the same person in the course of one transaction to be tried together. It does not, however, make a joint trial compulsory in every case involving rival versions of the same occurrence. Separate trials may lawfully be conducted, but each case must be decided on the evidence properly recorded therein. Where evidence relating to the cross-case is necessary for determining the responsibility of the accused, the Court must ensure that it is brought on record through the witnesses competent to prove it. Such evidence cannot be relied upon merely because it forms part of another judicial file. The parties must also be given an opportunity to test that evidence through crossexamination. Thus, the difficulty in the present case is not that the two cases were tried separately, but that material evidence relating to Mad No.24 was not properly examined.

10. This omission also requires consideration in the light of Article 10-A of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, which guarantees the right to a fair trial and due process. A fair trial is not confined to giving the accused an opportunity of _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz hearing. It also requires that criminal liability be determined through a fair examination of the evidence, with an effective opportunity to challenge material relied upon against the accused. In the present case, both parties claimed to have sustained injuries during the same occurrence. The medical evidence could establish the nature and extent of those injuries, but could not, by itself, determine which party was responsible for initiating the incident. That question required the learned trial Court to consider the ocular accounts alongside the medical evidence, site plans, recoveries and other relevant circumstances. Since the essential evidence of Mad No.24 was not properly brought on record, the learned trial Court could not examine the rival versions upon a complete evidentiary foundation. The omission was material to the fairness of the adjudication, particularly when the resulting judgment involved the conviction of the appellants.

11. The law provides a specific remedy for such a situation under Section 540 Cr.P.C., which reads as follows:— 540. Power to summon material witness, or examine person present.—Any Court may, at any stage of any inquiry, trial or other proceeding under this Code, summon any _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz person as a witness, or examine any person in attendance, though not summoned as a witness, or recall and re-examine any person already examined; and the Court shall summon and examine or recall and reexamine any such person if his evidence appears to it essential to the just decision of the case.

The provision empowers a Court to summon or recall a witness at any stage of the proceedings. More importantly, its latter part makes the exercise of that power obligatory where the evidence of a witness appears essential for a just decision. The learned trial Court was, therefore, competent to summon the witnesses connected with Mad No.24 and require the relevant documents to be proved in accordance with law. The purpose of this power is to enable the Court to reach a just conclusion on the basis of material evidence. It cannot be exercised merely to strengthen a weak prosecution case or to provide an additional opportunity to secure a conviction. The burden of establishing guilt beyond reasonable doubt remains upon the prosecution, irrespective of whether any witness is examined at its instance or summoned by the Court.

12. Reliance in this regard may be placed upon the judgment rendered by a learned Division _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz Bench of this Court in the case of “Zafarullah alias Zafrol v. The State through A.A.G. and others” (2022 PCr.L.J. 1098), wherein, while adjudicating upon an identical controversy involving cross-versions/rival cases stemming from the same occurrence, it was held as that:- "However, neither the remaining important documents of the cross case were exhibited in the present case nor the respective witnesses were examined. It was the duty of the defence to have brought on the record the relevant documents of the other file to the file of the present case. Even at the same time the trial Court as well as the prosecution were supposed to bring on the record the real facts of the case and all the available material which, in our view, have not been done."

"In absence of the important evidence/documents of the cross case, we are unable to adjudge the matter according to the settled principles of criminal justice. Thus, without discussing merits of the case lest it prejudice the case of either side and for doing substantial justice in the matter, remand of the case has become imperative. Therefore, this appeal is partially allowed, the impugned judgment is set aside and the case is remanded to the trial Court with directions to examine or re-examine all essential witnesses of the alleged cross-case (FIR No.55) as Court witnesses who authored the report, site plan, recovery memos and other relevant documents which in the opinion of the trial Court are essential for the just decision of the _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz case and bring the same on the file of the present case through the authors of those documents in accordance with law."

13. The principle laid down in the above judgment applies to the present case. Here too, two rival criminal cases arose from the same occurrence, but the evidence relating to the cross-case was not fully examined in the trial which resulted in conviction. The importance of that evidence lies in its direct connection with the circumstances of the occurrence. Without examining the relevant witnesses and documents of Mad No.24, the learned trial Court could not properly assess whether the prosecution version in FIR No.430/2021 had been established beyond reasonable doubt. In case of Zafarullah alias Zafrol (supra), the Division Bench considered a similar deficiency sufficient to set aside the conviction and remit the matter for examination of the essential evidence. The same course is appropriate in the circumstances of the present case.

14. Having examined the record in the light of the above principles, this Court finds that the conviction was recorded without proper consideration of material evidence necessary for resolving the rival versions of the occurrence. This deficiency is _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz significant because the identity of the aggressor and the individual responsibility of the parties could not be fairly assessed without examining the evidence relating to Mad No.24. The conviction, therefore, cannot safely be maintained in its present form. At the same time, the omission does not justify recording a finding of acquittal without first examining the material evidence. The guilt or innocence of the appellants must be determined by the learned trial Court upon a proper assessment of the evidence lawfully brought before it. Since the investigation and trials have already concluded, there is no necessity for fresh investigation or a de novo trial. A limited remand for recording the essential additional evidence and deciding the case afresh would meet the requirements of justice, in exercise of the appellate powers under Sections 423 and 428 Cr.P.C.

15. As regards connected Criminal Appeal No.196-A/2026, challenging the acquittal of Tasawar Nisar and Zohaib Nisar in Mad No.24, it is well settled that an acquittal strengthens the presumption of innocence and interference therewith is permissible only where the judgment suffers from material misreading or non-reading of evidence, perversity or substantial illegality. The deficiency identified in the _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz trial of FIR No.430/2021 does not, by itself, establish any illegality in the acquittal recorded in Mad No.24. Since the main case is being remanded for fresh adjudication, it would be appropriate to defer consideration of the connected acquittal appeal, leaving its merits open for independent determination in accordance with law.

16. The connected criminal revision filed by complainant Tasawar Nisar seeks enhancement of the sentence awarded to the appellants. Since the conviction and sentence are being set aside, there remains no subsisting sentence capable of enhancement. The revision has, therefore, become infructuous.

17. In view of the foregoing discussion, the instant Appeal is partially allowed, and the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence dated 25.09.2026 is hereby set aside. The case is remanded back to the learned trial Court with the direction to examine or reexamine the essential witnesses under Section 540 Cr.P.C. and bring on record the relevant site plans, recovery memos, medical reports and other material documents in accordance with law. Both parties shall be afforded an opportunity of cross-examination. Thereafter, fresh statements of the accused under _________________________________________________________________ Shahid/* (S.B.) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz Section 342 Cr.P.C. shall be recorded, as per law. The learned trial Court shall decide the case afresh on merits, within the period four months from receipt of this judgment.

18. The appellants, who are presently confined in jail, shall be treated as under-trial prisoners and shall be entitled to all facilities admissible under the law. Their earlier bail is hereby restored, and they shall be released on bail upon furnishing fresh bail bonds to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court, provided they are not required to be detained in any other case. The record shall be transmitted forthwith to the learned trial Court. The parties are directed to appear before the learned trial Court on 08.12.2026. However, the Connected Cr. A No.196-A/2026, challenging the acquittal recorded in Mad No.24, is adjourned sine die, whereas the connected Criminal Revision seeking enhancement of sentence is dismissed as having become infructuous.
Announced Dt.19.11.2026 JUDGE
